name: Obadiah
overview: Obadiah is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Joab and the son of Jehiel. He is noted for having accompanied Ezra during the return to Jerusalem, as recorded in Ezra 8:9. No tribal affiliation or additional personal details are provided beyond his lineage and role in this event.
namesAndTitles: The name Obadiah means 'servant [worshiper] of YHWH,' reflecting a devotion to the Lord. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but signifies a person dedicated to serving God, as noted in Ezra 8:9.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Obadiah is the son of Jehiel. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection and his descent from Joab.
scriptureSignificance: Obadiah's significance lies in his participation in the return of the exiles with Ezra, marking him as part of the faithful remnant committed to restoring worship and obedience to God in Jerusalem. His lineage from Joab and connection to Jehiel highlight his place within the community involved in this pivotal moment of restoration. Through his role, Obadiah exemplifies faithful service in the work of God's redemptive plan during the post-exilic period.
